_comment: api-mcp-adapter App Config. This app serves the endpoints listed in 'http' as ONE MCP server at POST /mcp, and every tools/call is a templated request the enclave makes with its own secrets. There are no tools by default: add an 'http' array (or rename '_example_http' below) and redeploy. An eyesoff-ai 'tools.http' block pastes in unchanged, which is the point; scripts/from-eyesoff-config.py does the split for you. Full field reference: the app's README.
_auth_comment: api_key is the key clients send as 'X-Api-Key: <key>' (the enclave.host gateway consumes 'Authorization', so a bearer never arrives). Reference a SECRET, never a literal: this file is public on-chain by CID. If the secret is not set the deployment LOCKS and says so, rather than serving your tools to whoever finds the URL.
_entry_comment: Each entry: name, description and JSON-Schema 'parameters' are what a model sees; 'url' is absolute and may carry {arg} placeholders (never in the host, which is refused, so a caller can never move the call to another server); 'method', 'headers' and a 'body' template whose whole-string "$arg" values are filled from the arguments. '$NAME' in a url or header is a deployment secret. A header whose whole value is "$user" carries the signed-in account, and that tool is hidden and refused unless the request names one. 'result' pulls the answer out: {"text": "<dot path>"} for a field, {"image": "<dot path>"} to return a picture. 'sources' ({"list","title","url"}) becomes citations. 'group', 'max_chars' and 'format' are passed to the client, which applies them.

_example_http.name: notes_read
_example_http.description: Read one note's full text by name.

_example_http.name: generate_image
_example_http.description: Generate an image from a text prompt. It is shown to the user directly; you never see it, so acknowledge it briefly.
